rule_descriptions.common-coding-style: Use when writing or reviewing code in any language -- naming, structure, error handling, and comment conventions.
rule_descriptions.common-testing: Use when adding or changing tests, or when a behavior change has no regression guard yet.
rule_descriptions.common-edit-safety: Use BEFORE editing files or running destructive shell/git commands -- tool selection, forbidden sed/regex rewrites, and how to verify an edit.
rule_descriptions.common-performance: Use when a change touches hot paths, allocations, frame timing, or whenever a slowdown is reported.
rule_descriptions.common-code-review: Use when reviewing a diff or PR -- five axes, severity labels, and the ~100-line change discipline.
rule_descriptions.rust-coding-style: Use when writing or reviewing Rust (.rs) -- ownership/borrowing, error types, iterator idioms, and clippy-clean patterns.
rule_descriptions.rust-testing: Use when adding Rust tests -- cargo test layout, property tests with proptest, and insta snapshots.
rule_descriptions.rust-security: Use when Rust code touches unsafe, FFI boundaries, or untrusted input -- SAFETY comments and audit expectations.
rule_descriptions.rust-hooks: Use when editing Rust lifecycle hooks or callbacks -- initialization order and teardown guarantees.
rule_descriptions.cpp-coding-style: Use when touching C or C++ headers, FFI shims, or the CMake consumption surface.
rule_descriptions.typescript-coding-style: Use when writing TypeScript (.ts) in bindings or web demo glue.
rule_descriptions.web-coding-style: Use when editing web demo pages (HTML/CSS/JS) or the page-level beacon wiring.
rule_descriptions.common-agents: Use when delegating to subagents or writing agent memory -- the execution gate and memory-update duties are non-negotiable.
rule_descriptions.common-development-workflow: Use when starting a feature, writing a commit message, or opening a PR -- the workflow and its gates.
rule_descriptions.common-docker: Use when a change runs in Docker or hits the network -- volume-mount performance, dependency caches, UDP port ranges.
rule_descriptions.common-hooks: Use when editing tool-approval or hook configuration -- hook types, auto-accept policy, todo hygiene.
rule_descriptions.common-lesson-memory: Use when extracting lessons after a failure or on a review request -- triggers, write targets, timing, entry quality.
rule_descriptions.common-patterns: Use when choosing a project skeleton or a cross-language pattern -- language depth lives in the per-language patterns file.
rule_descriptions.cpp-hooks: Use when wiring C/C++ build hooks or the native CI pipeline stages.
rule_descriptions.cpp-patterns: Use when designing C++ types -- RAII, rule of five/zero, value semantics, error-handling shape.
rule_descriptions.cpp-security: Use when C/C++ touches memory -- buffers, undefined behavior, static analysis coverage.
rule_descriptions.cpp-testing: Use when writing or running C++ tests -- framework, sanitizers, expected coverage.
rule_descriptions.python-coding-style: Use when writing Python (scripts, tooling) -- standards, immutability, formatting.
rule_descriptions.python-hooks: Use when editing PostToolUse hooks for the Python tool surface.
rule_descriptions.python-patterns: Use when shaping Python structure -- protocols, dataclasses as DTOs, context managers and generators.
rule_descriptions.python-security: Use when Python handles credentials or dependency scanning.
rule_descriptions.python-testing: Use when writing Python tests -- framework, coverage, test organization.
rule_descriptions.rust-patterns: Use when structuring Rust -- trait-based repositories, service layer, newtypes, enum state machines.
rule_descriptions.typescript-hooks: Use when editing TS/JS tool hooks (PostToolUse, Stop ordering).
rule_descriptions.typescript-patterns: Use when shaping TS code -- API response format, custom hooks, repository layer.
rule_descriptions.typescript-security: Use when TS/JS handles credentials or the agent support wiring.
rule_descriptions.typescript-testing: Use when writing TS/JS tests -- E2E shape and the agent-support path.
rule_descriptions.web-design-quality: Use BEFORE writing page or component code -- anti-template policy, worthwhile style directions, component checklist.
rule_descriptions.web-hooks: Use when ordering web tooling hooks -- PostToolUse, PreToolUse, Stop and their sequence.
rule_descriptions.web-patterns: Use when structuring web pages -- composition, state management, URL as state, data fetching.
rule_descriptions.web-performance: Use when a page feels slow -- Core Web Vitals targets, bundle budget, loading and image strategy.
rule_descriptions.web-security: Use when shipping web surfaces -- CSP, XSS prevention, third-party scripts, HTTPS headers.
rule_descriptions.web-testing: Use when testing web pages -- priority order, E2E shape, unit tests.

targets.label: trae
targets.notes: activation layer, gitignored; mcp only (Trae natively reads AGENTS.md and .agents/skills). optional = absent layer is SKIP. structured_compare = the IDE re-indents the file on save (D50 R1). mcp_launcher_absolute = Trae does not spawn MCP servers in the repo root, so the launcher must be an absolute path (legal here because this file is gitignored)

targets.label: qoder
targets.notes: activation layer, gitignored. Tiers proven by a runtime probe (2026-11-05, .omo/plans/2026-10-28-agent-audit-followups.md S6 Step 1): alwaysApply:true => always-on; alwaysApply:false + description => model-decision (fetchable on demand); no glob tier exists in this host -- globs / glob / type:glob produced nothing at all; a file with no frontmatter is not injected; .mdc and the <rule>/RULE.mdc layout are both read, so the codebuddy emitter is reused verbatim. rules_inherit_from keeps the 12 descriptions single-owned instead of forking the wording. optional = absent layer is SKIP (fresh clone / CI).
